text: Identify the result the arrangement is meant to deliver, then examine the elements and relationships that make it possible. A system may combine hardware, people, software, procedures, services and ongoing support. What it does depends on its interactions, not merely on whether every component exists. Defining a boundary helps distinguish what belongs to the design from external partners and operating conditions.

items: Name the intended outcome. You should see: One clear purpose. If not: Ask whose need the system serves.
List elements needed for that purpose. You should see: People, equipment, services, and support as needed. If not: Check whether any needed support was left outside.
Mark the boundary and outside connections. You should see: Each important outside link has a named role. If not: Review the operating environment.
Illustration: Individual devices may work, but the mission can fail when the radio receives no power.

text: Purpose, elements, and interfaces combine to produce system behavior.
Decide what success looks like for the whole arrangement before comparing individual components.
A component choice may still be appropriate when its effects on other parts are understood.
